messages:
Jess: noticed a 503 + 429 spike from the apiserver in eu-west1 starting ~08:12 UTC when the GPU pool autoscaled up
Avi: same, controller-manager leader flapped twice, pods showed Pending due to NodeAffinity while GPUs came online
Marco: etcd metrics show kvstore_p99 increased from 30ms -> 1.1s at 08:11:45, leader CPU jumped to 88%
Priya: logs on apiserver: `E08:12:16.452 apiserver.go:xxxx] apiserver request-handler error: etcdserver: mvcc: required revision has been compacted` — a bunch of retries afterwards
Jess: interesting — we also saw an uptick in prefix cache-misses; hit ratio dropped from 96% -> 61% during the spike
Avi: timeline looks like: GPU provisioning started -> control-plane watch fanout increased (more node object churn) -> cache invalidations -> etcd qps up -> leader CPU + apiserver latencies
Marco: can someone paste the deploy-bot output? did a node pool rollout overlap?
deploy-bot: release/infra/gpu-pool-autoscale v2.8.1 applied to eu-west1 at 08:10:02 by ci-pipeline (canary fraction 0.2)
Priya: we had a steady stream of kubelet RegisterNode calls while kube-proxy re-synced; that amplifies watch fanout a lot (each Node event fans out to controllers)
Jess: quick checks done: `kubectl get endpoints -n kube-system kube-apiserver -o wide` looks healthy but connection attempts spike from kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler
Marco: tried `curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8080/metrics | grep apiserver_request_latencies` on apiserver node — observed tail latencies 95th -> 2.4s
Avi: I started collecting pprof from etcd leader and apiserver, uploading to /tmp for postmortem (link: https://internal/pprofs/2298500000)
Priya: mitigation idea: reduce watch fanout by temporarily cordoning a subset of new nodes (so they don't Register until stable), or throttle kubelet register bursts at infra layer
Jess: short term I bumped apiserver replicas from 3 -> 5 in eu-west1 (scaled controlplane ASG) — seeing fewer 503s but still elevated latency
Marco: also opened a temporary exception in the egress rate limiter for etcd traffic from leader -> peers to reduce retransmit backpressure
Avi: controller-manager logs indicate leader election renewals were delayed: `failed to renew lease: context deadline exceeded` — likely caused by API server slow response to PUTs
Priya: config change we debated: increase `--max-requests-inflight` on apiserver to 800 and `--max-mutating-requests-inflight` to 200 to avoid queueing; risk is higher memory usage — watch OOM
Jess: agree — let's apply that as temporary, monitor memory/latency, then revert if it worsens
Marco: applied patch to kube-apiserver config at 08:22, rolling restart started (5 -> each node restarted sequentially). deploy-bot: rollout succeeded 08:27:41
deploy-bot: kube-apiserver config updated: --max-requests-inflight=800 --max-mutating-requests-inflight=200
Avi: after rollout apiserver p95 dropped from 2.4s -> 480ms, etcd p99 still slightly elevated at ~300ms but stabilizing
Jess: follow-ups: 1) add smoothing to autoscale to avoid simultaneous node registration 2) implement gate on kubelet register burst for new nodes 3) add apiserver qps autosafe on heavy watch fanout 4) run targeted etcd compaction verification (some mvcc compact messages noted)
Priya: cost/ops note: adding control-plane replicas had direct cost impact; estimated ~+12% to regional infra for the hour. We'll include in incident cost note and evaluate if we want standby replicas for busy scaling windows
Marco: opening an incident doc and assigning postmortem. I'll capture pprofs, metrics, and the rollout timeline in the doc
Jess: thanks — for now alerts that were noisy: `apiserver_5xx_rate`, `etcd_client_latencies_p95`, `controller_manager_leader_renew_failures`. Lowering alert sensitivity for duplicate alerts while we triage
oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2023-4553 (eu-west1 control-plane degradation). Owner: Marco. Priority: P2
Priya: will follow up with infra to add a 3-minute smoothing window to the GPU autoscaler to prevent bursts of RegisterNode events
Avi: assigning owners: etclat: Marco, apiserver flags + rollout: Jess, autoscale smoothing: Priya. Will reconvene in 2h for postmortem draft
Jess: resolved for now — keeping monitoring on for next 4 hours. If anyone sees regressions ping here or escalate to oncall
Marco: status update at 09:00 UTC: metrics hold steady, closing this thread into incident doc
